To get an object path we can use a DBus interface already existing somewhere.

For example you could make 2 configurations. The first one is `"Probe": "TRUE"` and then use that to probe the 
`xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.Board` interface
from the second configuration.

That way we will have an object path to associate to.
Done
We can also include the `busctl` output from `ObjectMapper` here to check that it picked up the association definition and created the association.
Done

Now in case of `Probe=True` there is no object path that we probed on. So i would assume the association definitions to be empty in that case.

From my understanding, associations are intended to link object paths so they should contain object paths and we cannot put just any string there.
No big deal, I deleted the handling of Probe=True

Why do we have `ProbePath` on DBus as part of the inventory item.

The association already tells us the object paths the configuration was probed on.
Removed.

`Topology::addBoard` is meant to receise exposes record json but in our case there is no configuration backing this feature.

So we may want to create a separate function in topology class to insert this information and call from here.
Introduced a seperate function for the job.

Can we have a small comment here as to what this map is representing.

e.g. "Mapping the inventory object path to the object path the configuration was probed on"
Done

We are always adding things to the map here but it never gets cleared and nothing is ever removed.

So the map will not represent the current state of probe associations anymore when a configuration is removed from DBus.
Done
No need to repeat the function name.
Done

'keeps track of the mapping between inventory items and the object paths they were probed on`.

The function does not create any association in the current patchset. It only populates the map.
Done
No need to repeat the `probePath` variable name. It will just bitrot when someone renames the variable.
Done

What happens in case there is multiple object paths responsible for the Probe.

For example

```
    "Probe": [
        "xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'BOARD_PRODUCT_NAME': 'Ventura RMC'})",
        "AND",
        "xyz.openbmc_project.FruDevice({'BOARD_INFO_AM4': 'hsc-xdp fsc-nct p24vsen-isl gndsen-isl p12vbrick-flex'})"
    ],
```

in `meta/ventura_rmc_hsc_xdp_fsc_nct_p24vsen_isl_gndsen_isl_p12vbrick_flex.json`.

Do the DBus interfaces in `Probe` statement always have to be on the same object path, and it makes no difference?
